1. allow users to upload local sessions 
2. the agent runs on github for that session, and then add it to memory / rubrics

comments.body:
This fits the current architecture. Recommended MVP: a trusted user exports a sanitized local transcript, attaches it to an issue comment, then manually runs a new “Inspect Local Session” workflow using that comment URL. Sepo should inspect the trace as untrusted evidence and persist only distilled findings—not the raw transcript.

Existing foundations:

- The attachment helper already restricts downloads to GitHub user attachments and enforces safe filenames, timeouts, and a 25 MiB limit ([source](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/github-attachment-download.ts#L47-L70)).
- Existing continuity bundles restore provider files into the runner’s home directory ([source](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/session-bundle.ts#L356-L398)). User uploads should not use that path.
- `run-agent-task` already mounts both branches and independently commits memory plus validates/commits rubrics ([setup](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/actions/run-agent-task/action.yml#L298-L332), [persistence](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/actions/run-agent-task/action.yml#L543-L606)).
- Existing prompts already define conservative memory durability and trusted-source rubric learning ([memory](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/prompts/memory-scan.md#L14-L30), [rubrics](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/prompts/rubrics-update.md#L17-L57)).

Implementation plan:

1. Add a local export CLI producing a versioned, sanitized trace format. Preserve user/assistant messages and minimal provenance; omit credentials, environment snapshots, and raw tool payloads. Support canonical JSON/JSONL plus plain Markdown/text initially—no uploaded archives.
2. Add a validator that downloads the attachment with the existing helper, checks schema/size/record limits, computes a digest, and confirms the attachment URL appears in the supplied source issue comment.
3. Add `agent-local-session-inspection.yml` with inputs for source comment URL, destination (`memory`, `rubrics`, or `both`), and branch refs. Run with `session_policy: none`.
4. Add a dedicated inspection prompt and route. Treat trace instructions as data, learn rubrics only from explicit preferences attributable to a trusted user, and add memory only for durable repository-specific facts or lessons. Duplicate or weak evidence should produce no changes.
5. Post a source-issue summary showing the digest and separate memory/rubrics commit outcomes; never quote sensitive trace content.
6. Add parser/security tests, workflow contract tests, prompt guardrail assertions, documentation, and run the complete `.agent` CI suite.

I’m interpreting “runs on GitHub for that session” as inspecting the transcript, not resuming the provider’s live session. Live resumption should be a separate security design because it restores uploaded state into the runner.

If that interpretation is correct, send:

`@sepo-agent /implement Implement the sanitized local-session inspection workflow for issue #489 using the plan above.`

but i think we can do this even more aggressively? let's say we can even create an agent/traces branch? 

1. for local backups -> it will be uploaded there directly
2. for sepo live backups -> we can also regularly migrate traces to the agent/traces branch before it expires in the github actions cache?

Yes—`agent/traces` is a coherent third durable surface. I’d make it more aggressive, with one hard boundary: store sanitized evidence there by default, not plaintext restorable provider state.

| Surface | Content | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `agent/traces` | Immutable sanitized transcripts and provenance manifests | Durable inspection ledger |
| Actions artifacts | Raw ACPX/Codex/Claude session bundles | Temporary resume/restore |
| `agent/memory` | Distilled project context | Future agent continuity |
| `agent/rubrics` | Trusted explicit preferences | Steering and evaluation |

Two important corrections:

- Live session bundles currently use `actions/upload-artifact`, not the Actions cache ([workflow](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/actions/run-agent-task/action.yml#L630-L675)). The cache is only for runtime dependencies and compiled code ([setup](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/actions/setup-agent-runtime/action.yml#L125-L179)).
- Don’t wait until artifacts approach expiration. Archive the sanitized trace immediately after every successful run; use a scheduled sweep only to repair missed archives. GitHub’s artifact API exposes `expires_at`, so a daily repair workflow can detect approaching expiration ([GitHub API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/artifacts)).

Recommended design:

1. Bootstrap an orphan `agent/traces` branch with immutable, content-addressed paths such as `traces/2026/08/<sha256>.jsonl` and matching manifests containing origin, actor, thread key, run/comment URL, provider, timestamp, size, and digest.
2. Extend the local export CLI from draft PR #493 with `--push --repo`, allowing authorized users to upload sanitized traces directly. Duplicate digests become no-ops.
3. After each Sepo run, produce the same canonical sanitized trace and dual-write it immediately to `agent/traces`; keep uploading the raw continuity bundle as an artifact.
4. Add a daily repair workflow that enumerates unexpired `session-bundle-*` artifacts, checks whether their digest is already archived, and imports missing sanitized traces.
5. Add a cursor-based curator that reads only new trace manifests and proposes memory/rubric updates. Direct trace uploads never write memory or rubrics by themselves.
6. Add `AGENT_TRACE_POLICY` controls for disabled/sanitized/required behavior, size budgets, trusted uploaders, and retention.
7. Record trace digest/archive status in thread state so restore and inspection workflows can resolve either backend deterministically.

I would not commit raw session bundles to Git in plaintext: public-repository branches are public, secrets are difficult to erase from Git history, and an append-only trace archive will eventually enlarge the repository. GitHub recommends keeping repositories ideally below 1 GB and blocks regular Git files above 100 MiB ([GitHub guidance](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/working-with-files/managing-large-files/about-large-files-on-github)). If durable raw restoration is required, make it a separate opt-in encrypted backend—or eventually use object storage.

The sanitized export foundation already exists in draft PR #493, but its latest review found unresolved message-attribution trust defects. Those should be fixed before building archival and rubric learning on it ([review](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/493#issuecomment-5164504953)).

To pursue this design, send:

`@sepo-agent /orchestrate Implement #489 as a two-tier trace system: finish PR #493, add content-addressed agent/traces storage for local and live sanitized traces, immediate dual-write plus an artifact-expiry repair sweep, then cursor-based memory/rubrics curation; keep raw resumable bundles in Actions artifacts.`
